card.name: Right before a past-tense verb
card.fires_on: Words that come right after a subject noun phrase and just before its past-tense verb, such as a relative word (that, which, who), a closing quote mark, or a comma. The next word is likely was, had, or a similar past verb.

modes.label: Relative word after noun
modes.description: That, which or who after a noun, introducing a clause whose verb comes next.
modes.example: taking advantage of any clear spot<< that>> would carry me towards the enemy.

modes.label: Quote or comma closing the subject
modes.description: A closing quotation mark or comma that ends the subject phrase just before the verb.
modes.example: The finding, at the time<<,>> was hailed as a significant new discovery,

modes.label: Adverb or verb inside subject
modes.description: A word within the subject phrase, such as an adverb or needed, with the main verb following soon.
modes.example: Initially, all a webmaster<< needed>> to do was submit a page, or

card.writes: It pushes the model toward past-tense was or had as the next word and away from Russian present-tense verb endings.
card.plain: It fires at the end of a subject phrase, when a past-tense verb like was or had is expected next.
